capabilities: Assign a loading mode (lazy on demand, lazy on layout ready, always enabled, always disabled) to each plugin
Register dummy commands that cache plugin command metadata and load the real plugin on first use
Bulk-edit loading modes in a searchable, sortable plugin table
Rebuild cached command and view type data via a maintenance action
Back up and reconcile changes to community-plugins.json made by Sync, Git, or manual edits
disambiguation: It does not provide on-demand content itself; it controls when other already-installed plugins get loaded.
extras: Manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. README warns it monkey-patches Obsidian's core, so Obsidian updates may break it; inline/embedded views such as Dataview inline queries are unsupported; plugins using setInterval/setTimeout or global hooks should use Lazy on layout ready.
intentEvidence: This project is based on the work by Alan Grainger
problem: Obsidian loads every enabled community plugin at startup, so a large plugin collection slows startup even when most plugins are rarely used.

relations.evidence: This project is based on the work by Alan Grainger

summary: Plugin manager that delays loading of installed plugins until their commands, views, or files are used, keeping Obsidian startup fast.
